sharedMapEvidence: There is no register map, so there is nothing to share — but the model identity does need evidence, and it exists. The vendor manual is titled 'Battery Capacity Meter MNBCM / MNBCMS' (P/N 10-188-1 Rev C, dated 12-23-14) and covers both part numbers in one document, so the retailer listing 'Battery Capacity Meter' and the listings for 'MNBCM' are the same product under MidNite's own product name. M
gotchas: No comms of any kind. Two wires — red to the bank positive after a fuse, black to negative. The manual specifies no port, no bus, no connector and no data output. This cannot become a driver, and no protocol document exists because there is no protocol.

Voltage-derived SOC from a fixed table: at 12 V, 11.65 V = 10% through 12.75 V = 100%, scaled ×2 / ×3 / ×4 for 24 / 36 / 48 V. Accurate only at rest. This is exactly the complaint already recorded against the MidNite SoC meter at this site in docs/INVENTORY.md ('Voltage-based; unreliable under load').

Auto-detects 12 / 24 / 36 / 48 V. Maximum input 70 V, reverse-polarity protected. Draws 12.5 mA average; the MNBCMS draws 6 mA (0.07 W at 12 V) with the LEDs switched off. Requires a DC-rated fuse or breaker of no more than 2 A in the positive lead.

Battery chemistry is set by a jumper on the PCB, not in software: Gel = jumper on the two left pins, AGM = two right pins, Flooded = no jumper. Confirming that needs someone to read the part number off the unit on the wall — it is not established here, and the catalogue should not merge
unmappedReports: 'Battery care' state — three LEDs meaning fully charged / not fully charged for 1 week / not charged for 2 weeks or more. No MetricKind covers staleness-of-last-full-charge, and no DeviceKind covers a device whose only output is a lamp. Readable by eye only., The 10-LED arc is labelled state of charge but is a fixed voltage lookup, not a coulomb count. If it were ever digitised it would be `state-of-charge` in name only, and would disagree with a shunt-derived one under load.
